Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusMeasured over the game's art: dark forest greens #192f29 19% and #375d56 10%, near-white #eef2f0 9% (smoke, numerals), brick brown #8d3d17 6%, warm yellow #f3d07a 6%, sky blues #6498bd 6% and #a7cfe1 4%, straw #efdaae 2%. Zeus vs Hades POPTwo opposed families and one shared metal. Zeus and the base game: cyan and blue (#22efff, #2b7cf2, #3986ce, #324382). Hades and free spins: red, orange and dark crimson (#8e1f15, #540e19, #d92d11, #f49419). Gold (#f9ea77, #f49419) trims every symbol and frame on both sides. Measured over the game's own art: vivid (saturation 63%), mid-tone, warm 54% against cool 40%.
Lighting
GameLighting
Cash EruptionFire is the light everywhere: the hall is lit from below and in front as if by firelight, the fireball and flames are self-lit, the wild is lit warm from the fire behind her. The regular symbols alone have a neutral studio light from the upper left with a star glint.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandNight scene lit from inside the picture by lamps; objects are top-lit with hard gloss. Glow is kept as separate additive layers and outline sprites (hat glow, wedge glow, row highlight), not painted in. On screen the reel window is the darkest area and the wheel and lawn the brightest.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinObjects are lit from the upper left or front with a red-orange rim from below right; the backdrop's fire lights from the bottom of the screen. Lamps, coins' flames and all effects are self-lit.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinSelf-lit neon everywhere; there is no light source in a scene because there is no scene. Objects are lit from the top or top-left with a blue rim from below, as if standing on a lit sign. Glow circles behind the board make the centre the brightest area.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsDaylight, even and shadowless, for the base game; the file named for the free game is the same stadium at night under six floodlights. Objects are top-lit with hard gloss. Glow is kept as separate layers and outline sprites. On screen the reel window is the darkest area and the pitch the brightest.
Triple Cash EruptionSymbols are lit from the top left with a soft shadow below. Everything that pays is self-lit: fireballs, lava, halos and frames glow past their own edges. Both backgrounds are lit from one hot source in the middle (the crack in the temple wall, the lava lake) and fall dark at the sides, which keeps the panels and the board readable.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelTop and top-left light on every object (measured: top 91, top-left 53, top-right 41 of the parts with a readable light side). Each symbol ships a 'Light' and a 'Light Hit' copy of itself as an additive layer for its flash, plus thin light sweeps. The hall is lit warm from windows and a ceiling lightbox against cool walls; the bonus room is lit by its own gold.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedAlmost everything is self-lit: neon, lamps behind plates, fire. Symbols have a conventional upper-left light and a warm halo. The backdrop's light comes from one vanishing point behind the cabinet.
Capital GainsA plain light from above on nearly everything (top on 354 parts measured, top-right 81, top-left 55), with white streak highlights on gold. No scene lighting, no cast light between objects. Lightning and the vault symbol's landing flash are self-lit.
CleopatraNo scene lighting. Each object carries its own frontal highlight; the cabinet has banded reflections like polished metal; the Sphinx (scatter and Big Win) and the fire are self-lit. The backdrop is a plain vertical gradient with no sun or lamp.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarTwo lights in the base scene: warm lantern light from the stalls and the ground, cool dusk from above. Symbols are lit softly from the upper left with their smoke as a back light. Lamps glow from inside. The cave is lit by blue shafts from above.
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinObjects are lit from the top or top-right with a green bounce from below, as if standing in the clover field. The backdrop is darkest in the middle so the board glows against it. In the feature scene the light source is the rainbow ribbon itself.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinDiffuse daylight from above through mist in the base scene; a low orange sun and coloured haze in the bonus. Game pieces are lit from the top with their own highlights and do not take the scene's light. The statue is lit from above until its mouth and eyes light it from inside.
Huff N Puff Money MansionDaylight from above on a clear day; objects are top-lit with hard gloss. Glow is kept as separate additive layers and outline sprites (hat glow, frame pulses, plate highlights), not painted in. The background is repainted for evening and night, with lit windows and lantern pools at night, and the prize plates have day and night versions to follow it.
Money Gong EmperorOne top light on everything (measured from the top on 174 parts, top-right on 32, top-left on 19) with specular glints on the gold; the backgrounds are dark with a low glow, so the gold objects are the light of the screen. The base reel backing is the darkest surface (#550202, brightness 0.07).
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusDaylight from the upper right in the base scene and a low sunset behind the hills in the special scene; props and plates are lit from the upper left; characters have a warm key and a thin cool rim. Nothing glows by itself except a plate being boosted.
Zeus vs Hades POPEach side is lit by its own element: cool cyan light from lightning on Zeus pieces, warm light from fire on Hades pieces, usually against the opposite temperature in the shadows (purple-blue shadows on warm skin). Bevels are top-lit. Lightning, fire, frame edges and eyes are emissive and drawn as separate additive layers, so glow is a layer, not paint.
Ambience
GameAmbience
Cash EruptionHot, enclosed and ceremonial in the base game; hotter in the free spins; vast and ominous in the bonus, under a red spiral sky. Over it sits the plain cheer of a classic fruit machine: the theme is a dressing on familiar symbols, not a story.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandCheerful, loud and crowded, as the base-game screens show: the wheel, the rolling sign, six plaques and the logo all compete around a dark reel window, and the calm garden is reduced to a green and blue margin. The wolf is a comic villain, present in the base game only as a tail swishing under the reels. The pace of wins and features is not known from this run.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinA furnace and a ticket office: hot, rich, a little nostalgic. The base game is half fire and half cool purple; the cash bonus turns the backdrop to gold and purple postcards, the jackpot bonus to fire across the whole screen.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinHigh voltage, arcade and motorsport: fast, loud, synthetic. The mood comes from motion of light, not from a place or a story.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsMatch day with a full house: cheerful, loud, busy. The wheel, two goals, five plaques and an animated logo crowd the top of the screen around a calm dark reel window. The villain is a joke: the wolf's threat is a whistle. A win of ten times the bet was marked by a gold light burst and a one-line caption, no more.
Triple Cash EruptionFamiliar and safe on the reels, loud and hot around them. The base game is an expectant temple chamber; the bonus drops into the crater, darker and redder, where gold numbers in fire rings are the only bright things. The opening is a short disaster film: eruption, flaming rocks at the camera, title, wipe to yellow.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelFriendly greed: money as sweets and toys, nothing sinister about the bank. The base game is a calm night hall with a mascot watching from the top of the reels; the bonus is the inside of the vault, all gold. The shared Super Wheel brings a louder, studio-lights mood from outside the theme.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedA machine in a dark club, humming with neon, that catches fire when a feature starts. The base game is cool and purple, Free Spins and the intro are orange and red; the cabinet itself does not change.
Capital GainsBright, clean and blunt: the promise is money itself. Calm in the base game, hotter by colour alone in the free spins, and charged when the lightning locks the green discs in the bonus.
CleopatraOpulent, calm and familiar: a jewel box at dusk. The base game is cool purple around warm gold; the free spins heat the whole screen to crimson and age the reels to tan papyrus. Nothing moves until a win, so the game feels like a machine rather than a scene.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarA warm, rich evening market with a secret in it; friendly rather than mysterious, because the genie smiles and the smoke is pink. The cave is the cold, magical counter-scene.
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinCosy, lucky and good-humoured: a pub sign in a clover patch at night. The feature scene is the same place enchanted, not a different world.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinAn expedition that has found the temple: humid, hushed and green at first, with danger shown as beauty (jewel snakes, a sleeping statue). The bonus is heat and treasure: red walls, gold underfoot, the statue's eyes burning.
Huff N Puff Money MansionSunny, proud and busy, as the base-game screens show: the mansion fills the picture behind the reels, prize plates glow on its roof, four plaques stand at the left and the logo at the right, and the reel window is the one dark area. Wins in the base game are modest: a line of text names the ways at the foot of the reels, the wolf is boxed in gold, and a larger win ($12.00 at a $2.00 bet) puts gold digits on a flare. The wolf is a comic villain who appears in the base game only as a reel symbol. The pace of features is not known from this run: none came in about 32 spins.
Money Gong EmperorFestive, lucky and rich: New Year firecrackers, coins, pots of gold and a laughing emperor. Calm in the base game, where the screen is a dark red wall with gold furniture; the bonus spins turn the board itself gold.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusSunny, rustic and good-humoured. The base game is a building site in a meadow at midday; the intro shows the finished village at sunset with the wolf waiting. Threat is played as comedy.
Zeus vs Hades POPA playful rivalry rather than a solemn myth: loud, bright, friendly menace. The base game is an airy storm sky, calm between flashes; free spins is a hot, busy underworld of lava falls, chains and stone pillars. POP moments switch to soap bubbles and pastel rainbow, closer to a casual mobile game than to the Greek set.
Shapes
GameShapes
Cash EruptionRound, full, simple silhouettes for the symbols; rectangles and thin rails for every frame; the step-fret (a squared spiral) as the one ornament, repeated on frames, button rings, the coin, the ribbon ends, the cell pattern and even the watermelon seeds.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandRound and chunky everywhere: domed hats, circular saws and coins, rounded topiary, bubble letters. Sharpness is kept for the saw teeth, the wolf's muzzle and ears, and spark bursts.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinCircles (coins, wheel, boiler door, fire rings), the perforated ticket rectangle, rounded plaques with one cut corner, a thin square frame, fat slab-serif letters.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinThe slanted parallelogram (plates, backplates, frame corners), the chevron (board pattern, meter fill, boost arrows), the lightning zigzag (logo, letters' notches, the container's ends, the effects) and the faceted diamond. Circles appear only on the Wild and the coin.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsRound everywhere: balls, coins, cups, domed buttons, bubble letters, puffs of smoke. Points are kept for the wolf's muzzle and ears, the pennant wedges of the wheel and star ornaments.
Triple Cash EruptionRound and soft for everything collectable (fruit, bell, globes); square for everything structural (cells, frames, plates); the volcano cone is the one triangle and it is used as the game's badge. Frames are hairlines; the reel board has almost no body of its own.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelCircles and fat rounded squares: the pig is nearly a sphere, coins and wheels repeat it, tiles and panels have wide radii, letters are inflated. The snout (an oval with two holes) is the game's mark and is stamped on coins, bars, the case, the hammer, the vault and the carpet.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedThe seven above all: as symbol, jackpot plaque silhouette, win plate, 3D block and logo. Around it a pinched cabinet outline, chevrons, diamonds on the win lines, thin dotted bulb lines, fat slab letters.
Capital GainsRound and heavy: discs, coins, the vault wheel, the sack, the ring of the vault chamber. Rounded square tiles for high symbols. Slab-serif letters. The background's only ornament is banknote engraving: guilloche curves and scrollwork.
CleopatraSquare opaque cells in a strict grid; a symmetrical shrine frame with a curved cornice, two lotus columns and a boat-shaped base with fan prows; round beads and round buttons; the lotus fan as the repeating ornament (on the letters, the logo, the cabinet, the plaque).
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarRound and generous: bottle-bellied lamps, dome buttons, coins, cushion and heart-shaped gems, fat rounded royals. The frame answers with thin straight rails ending in curls. Smoke puffs and spirals soften every edge.
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinThe heart-shaped clover leaf is the module: backdrop leaves, the coin's stamp, the Scatter, the pipe's badge, the hat, the particles. Round bellies (pots, mug, barrel, coins, the character) against a thin wavy frame line; the curled scroll for jackpots; the arc for rainbows. The only sharp shape is the Booster arrow.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinDiamond snake heads and shield-shaped hoods; trapezoid plates in stepped-fret frames; slanted slab letters; round sun coins with spikes; square spiral frets on every frame end, lock plate and letter serif. The fret and the snake are the two repeated marks: the Wild, the win line's end, the win plate's ornament, the frame's corner and the opening wipe are all snakes.
Huff N Puff Money MansionRound and chunky everywhere: domed hats, coins, rounded topiary, bubble letters, pill buttons. Straight edges belong to the house: bricks, frames, plates, the hairline reel frame. Sharpness is kept for the wolf's ears and teeth, sparks and shards.
Money Gong EmperorCircles everywhere: gong, coins, money balls, jackpot discs, round buttons, the ring in the background, the bonus wheel. Around them, cloud scrolls and a Greek-key band as the two ornaments, and pill-shaped plaques for every figure. The lettering is the one angular element.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusRound and soft everywhere: balloon letters, fat tools, plump pigs, puffed clouds and bushes. The pig's snout (an oval with two dots) is the repeated mark, on every letter, the tape measure, the hard hat, the toolbox, the coin and the reel panel's watermark. Square frames are kept for the Wilds and houses only.
Zeus vs Hades POPRounded and chunky throughout, with angular accents (spikes, zigzag lightning, flames) reserved for power and danger. Frames are thin rails with Greek-key corners; figures break out of their frames.

Typography
GameTypography
Cash EruptionThe logo is heavy slab-serif capitals with a yellow-to-red gradient, a flame texture and a dark red extrusion; FREE SPINS and WILD are drawn in the same bevelled manner. Everything else is live text in Oswald (Bold, Regular and Light are embedded): condensed capitals in yellow or peach for labels and figures, and flat tier colours for the prize meters. The values on the fireballs are a black condensed bitmap font with an orange edge, in two sizes.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandDisplay lettering is drawn art: the logo gives each word its own material (wood HUFF, bubble PUFF, chrome GRAND), and prize and feature words are heavy rounded capitals with bevel, outline and rim, coloured by tier. Words are swapped as whole sprites for Spanish (PREMIO for JACKPOT). Running text is Noto Sans as twelve distance-field font pages, with Frutiger Neue in the provider's frame; both are the provider's.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinDrawn lettering in one family of Western slab serifs: black on gold for the logo, fire-filled for WILD, coloured enamel for the jackpot words, purple, blue and red with gold outlines for the win tiers, cream with a red edge for the splash sentences. One bitmap numeral font, purple with a gold rim. Everything else is the provider shell's Poppins (Regular, SemiBold, Bold).
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinHeavy slanted capitals throughout, in two related faces: a wide italic sans with chrome bands for the logo, WILD and BOOST, and the condensed Anton for numbers, jackpot names, win tiers and captions (gold two-band numerals with a red-brown side; a white set for small counts). The low symbols 10 to A are lettering too, cut by a bolt. Small interface text is the provider shell's Poppins (Regular, SemiBold, Bold).
Huff N Lots Of GoalsDisplay lettering is drawn art. The logo gives each word its own material and strikes PUFF out with a black brush stroke in favour of GOALS!. Prize and feature words are heavy rounded or slanted italic capitals with bevel, outline and rim, coloured by tier. Words are swapped as whole pictures for Spanish. Running text on screen is the provider's: Noto Sans as distance-field pages, with Jost and Outfit also shipped and Frutiger Neue in the provider's frame.
Triple Cash EruptionThe logo and the labels MULTIPLIER, COLLECT, DOUBLE and the jackpot names are one flared serif display face with bevel and gold rim, coloured by meaning. Win amounts use a bitmap font of marbled gold serif numerals; fireball values use a second bitmap font, very condensed black figures with a yellow and orange outline. Five font files are embedded for running text (QTFrizQuad Bold, Noto Sans Condensed Bold, an Oswald cut with currency glyphs, and the provider's Lato and Gilroy).
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelAll display words are painted lettering (logo, WILD, COLLECT, BONUS, the win tiers, prize names). Running text and numbers are set by the client: 53 of its 82 text styles lead with Borsok and Alegreya Sans Black, in cream (#fffef0) with a navy stroke (#140d49) for the big-win title, as its text-style file states. Thirteen font files ship; the Helvetica, Tahoma, Roboto, Barlow and Arial Black ones serve the provider's interface (inference from the style lists).
777 Hot Reels MegachargedOne voice: fat Western slab serifs. Drawn words for the logo, WILD, FREE SPINS, the jackpot names and the win tiers (gold to orange with a dark blue shadow); three bitmap numeral fonts from the provider's shared font store (UltraGold large, UltraActive and UltraInactive small). The help, the buttons and the balance line are the shell's Poppins.
Capital GainsThe logo is gold slab-serif capitals on two arches with a red-brown extrusion and a laurel; MONEY CHARGE is white-violet italic capitals over yellow JACKPOTS on a purple extrusion; WILD is cream western slab lettering; the disc values are cream slab numerals baked into each picture. Help pages set live text in red-orange outlined serif small capitals. 25 font files are embedded (among them Cinzel, Alfa Slab One, Bodoni, Trajan Pro, Bebas Neue, Roboto, Myriad Pro, Dollar Bill); which of them this game draws with was not traced, and a list this long reads as a provider's shared set (inference).
CleopatraThe wordmark is drawn: red capitals with a yellow inner line, a blue band and a gold rim, the C and the R enlarged, in the same comic manner as the face. The words on symbols (SCATTER, BONUS, DOUBLE) are fat cartoon capitals in red-to-yellow or red on violet. Everything else is live text in two embedded sans-serif fonts, Lato Bold and Roboto Regular: yellow for the free-spin messages, blue capitals for BIG WIN, white amounts, orange labels and green win figures on the meter bar. The paytable is a plain white web page with a blue-headed table.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarFour lettering families, all gold-based. The wordmarks: Mystery of the Lamp in a gold storybook serif with swashes, Secret Bazaar in red and gold slab capitals. The lamp words (Collect, Jackpot, Ignite) in a yellow decorative script with coloured 3D sides. The prize titles in a round seventies-style script, one colour each. Numerals in a tall fat Didone-like serif as bitmap fonts: gold chrome with a coloured edge for each prize, pink chrome for wins, ivory, yellow and orange for coin values. Big-win words are plain fat sans capitals in gold on a deep layered extrusion. Labels (TOTAL BET, WIN, BALANCE) are live text in Oswald; Yeseva One is embedded too.
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinFour voices. The logo and jackpot names: gold serif capitals with a brown side. WILD, SCATTER, BOOST, FREE SPINS and the other headlines: a curly western poster face in yellow and orange with a red rim; captions in the same face in white with a wine outline, written as rhymes. Win tiers: tall flared capitals, dark with a neon outline. Numbers: the provider's bitmap fonts, Ultra in cream and gold (jackpot values, win amounts) and in purple and gold, and Ravie in yellow with a rainbow side (the Spin Progress counter). The low symbols 10 to A are fat slab serifs in single colours. Small interface text is the shell's Poppins (Regular, SemiBold, Bold).
Serpent Gold Hold And WinDrawn words in slanted comic capitals with a dark outline for jackpots, win tiers and feature messages, each in its tier's or snake's colour. The logo is separate: spaced serif capitals in snake skin, gold and red. Numbers come from three bitmap fonts of the provider's shared store: Rubik Mono One in gold with a deep wine extrusion (ladder multipliers, win amounts), Blambot FX Pro Heavy in jade with a gold rim (the value on a Golden Coin, as the screens show), Anton italic in gold (the collector counters). The shell's Poppins sets the help, buttons and balance line.
Huff N Puff Money MansionDisplay lettering is drawn art: the logo gives each word its own material (riveted gold HUFF, hazard-tape N', bubble PUFF, comic 3D block MONEY MAN$ION), and prize and feature words are heavy rounded capitals with bevel, outline and rim, coloured by tier. Multiplier numbers are lettered sprites in a normal and a highlighted state. Running text is Noto Sans as distance-field font pages (four styles loaded), with Frutiger Neue in the provider's frame; both are the provider's.
Money Gong EmperorThe logo is heavy angular faux-brush capitals in bevelled yellow gold with a deep red extrusion. Jackpot names and MONEY GONG BONUS are drawn in the same faux-brush manner; two such faces are embedded (Gang of Three and Nuku Nuku), which is probably where they come from (inference). The three feature words are rounded poster capitals, one colour each. Running text is live Noto Sans (Black, Condensed Black, Condensed Bold, Regular) with Passion One. Figures are bitmap sets drawn per place: white for the bonus spins, magenta and gold for ball values, brown-lacquer and yellow for the Money Gong Bonus.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusTwo voices. Drawn balloon capitals with uneven baselines for the logo, the jackpot names and the win tiers, each word in its own colour; a fat rounded numeral face from the provider's shared font store in white (MarvinRound, on the ladders) and gold (MarvinRoundYellow, for jackpots and wins). HOLD & WIN and its rule line use the rounded face. The help, buttons and balance line are the shell's Poppins.
Zeus vs Hades POPDisplay lettering is drawn art, not type: ice-blue faceted ZEUS, gold flaming HADES and a gold bubble POP in the logo; bevelled gold words for the win tiers; extruded letters with a gold rim for A, K, Q and J. Seventeen typefaces are embedded for running text and numbers, most of them the provider's interface faces.
Motion
GameMotion
Cash EruptionNo skeletons: the game's own art is animated as Flash-style timelines at 30 frames a second (the files call them view-builder animations) over still pictures, with short frame sequences for fire. A winning symbol gets an outline glow, a spark and a looping 30-frame flame; the fireball boils over 30 frames; the Free Spins volcano throws lava in 30 frames over three stills of rising brightness; the full-reel wild moves only her headdress (13 frames), lips, brows and earrings, with two 27-frame flames at her hands. On a win every symbol off the line is dimmed and the winning cells get a sparkling frame, with the line amount in a small black box. Anticipation is a six-frame burning outline around a reel or a cell. Coins on a win are a particle emitter over a six-frame coin. The four Spine 4.1.24 skeletons among the captured files belong to a promotional overlay of the demo's host (a vault and raccoon theme), not to this game.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandSeen in the real frames: the two wheel rings turn slowly, the 3D sign above rolls from plate to plate, the wolf's tail swishes under the reels (1.33 s animations in the file), and on the one spin the spin button becomes a white stop square. Everything else is read from the files: eleven Spine 4.1.24 skeletons with symbol landings of 1.3 to 3.3 s and wins of 2 to 3 s, the wolf's pop-up (3.1 s in, 6.8 s loop) and blow (1.5 s in, 4.2 s loop), houses that build in 1.2 s and are blown away in 1.0 s, feature banners of 1.8 s, a 1.75 s caution-tape transition and a four-tier big win whose intro grows from 0.4 to 3.1 s. Faces, destruction and wind are drawn frame sequences (up to 89 frames; the three wind sheets total 137). Sprite sheets state 24 frames a second. No skeleton frame is shown in this report: the project's drawing tool does not read Spine 4.1 correctly.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinAll motion is Spine 4.2.43: 41 skeletons in one file, most of them scene layers and effects, moving still pictures and 25 hand-drawn frame sequences (445 frames: fire, glints, a turning coin and ticket). The train is one picture with animated wheel, rods, highlights and sparks. Seen in play: a fire sweep after START, coins thrown on the pile, the train driving across the reels into the bonus, coin and ticket showers, fire inside the live jackpot frame. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer is written for Spine 3.7.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinAll motion is Spine 4.2.43: 54 skeletons in one bundle file, moving, scaling and tinting still pictures, plus 14 hand-drawn frame sequences (278 frames), of which eight are lightning (150 frames), three are the diamonds' turn (75), and the rest a coin, a win-line bolt and a plate border. Seen in play: the red beams sweeping behind the board all the time; an opening sequence in which two large Boosters and then a large red diamond appear over the reels and charge the plates; a Booster on the reels growing to cover the board when it fires; plate values jumping with a flash; white-blue lightning crackling along the frame and around locked diamonds; coins flying from a diamond up to a plate; a lightning bolt along a paying line with the amount in gold numerals; in the bonus a yellow flash that turns the stage gold, diamonds blurring through single cells, bolts carrying prizes from the plates to the diamonds, and BIG WIN with a coin shower. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer is written for Spine 3.7.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsSeen in the real frames: the wheel stands at a different wedge in every frame; the logo animates (a ball rolls through GOALS!, PUFF pops under its strike); reels blur on the spin and the spin button becomes a stop square; a win flashes a wide gold burst behind the amount and dims the losing symbols; a collected red ball sends a rope of cream smoke diagonally up the reels to the red goal, with a puff where it leaves and a brighter puff where it arrives; a wheel symbol sends rainbow sparks up to the wheel, where a wedge flares gold. Read from the files only: twelve Spine skeletons (4.1.24, three exported from 4.2.43) with ball landings of 3.25 s, a 1.67 s wolf win, the wolf's pop-up (3.1 s in, 6.8 s loop) and blow (1.5 s in, 4.2 s loop), trophies that build in 1.2 s, feature panels of 1.8 s, a 1.4 s transition and a four-tier big win whose intro grows from 0.7 to 3.1 s. Effects are drawn sequences at the 24 frames a second the sheets state, the longest a 165-frame dust blast. No skeleton frame is shown in this report: the project's drawing tool does not read Spine 4.1 correctly.
Triple Cash EruptionThirteen Spine 4.0 skeletons (binary) drive the scene, but most of what moves is frame sequences inside them: 30-frame loops for each fireball and each flame border, 30-frame fire frames for wins and anticipation, 22 to 38 frame bursts for hits, landings and eruptions, and 20 burning frames per letter of the win words. Seen in play: reels spin as vertical smears; a win dims the board, puts fire frames on the winning cells and counts a gold number up; a fireball flies from its cell to the volcano of its colour and the lava on that cone rises; at the trigger all three volcanoes erupt, rocks fly at the camera and the screen burns to the bonus, where two 5x3 reel sets respin and lock orange fireballs with values.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelSkeletal: 64 Spine 3.8.99 skeletons, most of them short (0.83 s) bounce, win and collect moves on symbols built from a handful of parts, with longer idles for the mascot (4.17 s) and the scene (4.67 s). The signature move is the smash: a pig cracks, flies apart in 14 pre-cut shards and leaves a money heap. Frame sequences are kept for what a rig cannot do: the vault door (31 frames), spinning coins (18 a colour), gems (12 each), sparkles. The five intro pages are video clips. Curves in this Spine version are not read by the drawing tool, so the frames here show poses with linear easing.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedAll motion is Spine: 46 skeletons in two bundle files (44 in 4.2.43, two particle layers in 4.1.24), most of them scene layers and effects moving still pictures, with 22 hand-drawn frame sequences (398 frames: outline traces, fire, lightning, tumbling gems, a turning coin, the logo burning). Seen in play: the logo breaking up among coins after START, neon frames breathing, 777 blocks drifting behind the cabinet, cyan arcs on the frame and bolts at the jackpots, a gold seven flying from a Wild to the plaques, a lightning column on the last reel before a trigger, three sevens turning red on the splash, fire across the screen into Free Spins, Wilds locking, a BIG WIN and a MINOR jackpot win with gold rays and coins. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer is written for Spine 3.7; assembled and motion pictures are absent for that reason only.
Capital GainsFrame sequences only: no skeleton and no Spine file is shipped, so the empty assembled folder says nothing more than that. 45 sequences hold 854 frames: every symbol has a pre-rendered win animation (14 frames for the diamond, 24 for the other high symbols, 38 for each low symbol), the wild and the vault also a landing animation, the vault door swings open in 50 frames, lightning runs in 14 looping sets (276 frames, the largest), and coins and gems tumble in 24 frames each for the big win. Symbols mostly stay in place while a highlight crosses them; the energy comes from flashes and lightning, not from deforming art.
CleopatraNo skeletons and no timelines in the files: all animation is frame by frame, as full pictures. The wild has an 80-frame sequence in which the cell turns gold and two hands cross and open over the logo plate to show DOUBLE (and a second 80-frame version that keeps the logo); the Sphinx has 40-frame sequences in which the face glows, flames rise and SCATTER or BONUS wipes in; the Big Win is a 40-frame glow pulse of a Sphinx over a plaque with a counting number; the transition into and out of the free spins is 32 frames of fire inside a gold frame on black; a payline bead gets a 30-frame sparkle. The regular symbols do not animate: a win greys every other cell, frames the winning cells in the line's colour, draws the line to its bead and shows the amount in a small black tag (seen on the screens). The backdrop and cabinet never move.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarSpine 4.0 skeletons throughout (18 binary skeleton files, each with an opaque and an alpha page), mixing rigged parts with short frame sequences. The tools here read only JSON skeletons of older versions, so none was drawn, and the 10 skeletons counted at the top of this report are JSON files of a promotional overlay loaded by the demo host (prize tickets, chests, cards), not this game's. What follows is from the frame sequences, the names in the files and the real screens. Reels use pre-blurred copies of every symbol. Gems land wrapped in white lightning and send small gems up to their lamp, whose gold pile grows in three steps. The wild is a rolled carpet that unrolls over 39 frames to show WILD or 2X. Wins darken the board, put a magenta neon frame with a running light on each winning cell and count the amount in pink digits. The genie is a rig with IK that sways over a billowing smoke column, her hands glowing. Smoke (two puffs, many tints) loops behind the logo, the lamp words and the prize plaques. The big-win words are built letter by letter in five tiers; a coin stream and a spinning lamp are the transitions (inference from their skeletons; not reached in play).
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinAll motion is Spine 4.2.43: 64 skeletons in one bundle file, plus 15 hand-drawn frame sequences (290 frames): five of white sparkle and smoke (112 frames), two of rainbow (45), two of white bursts (33), two of the pots (34), three coin and coin-shine sequences (45) and the GRAND highlight (21). The leprechaun is a 55-bone rig with separate eyes, brows, moustache, coat halves and limbs; the mug's effect has 51 bones; the big-win banner 92. Seen in play: the leprechaun standing large in front of the board as the game opens; a full mug over a reel and beer running down whole reels as stacked WILDs with foam on top; coins dropping from Golden Coins towards the pots; a thin line across a winning row with the amount in cream and gold numerals; FEATURE UNLOCKED over a small copy of the board when the Spin Progress counter reaches zero; the 10 FREE SPINS splash over a white burst; a rainbow wash across the whole screen into the purple scene; a large mug with WILD over the board before Wild Reels; +5 FREE SPINS on a retrigger; BIG WIN on its wooden plaque over a violet haze with Golden Coins tumbling across the screen. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer is written for Spine 3.7.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinAll motion is Spine: 57 skeletons in one bundle file (47 in 4.2.40, 6 in 4.2.42, 4 in 4.2.43), with 29 frame sequences (515 frames: the coin's turn, a lava flow, fire, white glints fitted to each letter, word and plate, sparks, mist, two shatters). Seen in play: snake bodies wiping the intro away; the three collector frames arriving and the red Snake unlocking under a blue sparkling splash; coins flying from each Golden Coin to the statue, whose mouth and eyes turn red; clusters bound in a gold chain with a 3-2-1 lock disc; win lines in gold with a snake-head end; a gold win amount with a coin shower; the temple walls sliding in for the bonus. Read from the files only: jackpot wins, the big-win tiers, the Clone and Double Snakes in action. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer cannot draw Spine 4; assembled and motion pictures are absent for that reason only.
Huff N Puff Money MansionSeen in the real frames: the loading cards slide in turn; reels turn with a vertical blur and the spin button becomes a white stop square; hard hats land on glowing backings; Construction Pigs rise over a reel; the deed lands larger than its cell; a win shows a strip of text, a gold box on the wolf and, when larger, gold digits on a flare. Everything else is read from the files: 19 Spine 4.1.24 skeletons with hat landings of 1.3 to 3.0 s and wins of 2.0 s, the Construction Pig's pop-ups of 0.3 to 1.0 s, the wolf's blow in stages of 0.3 to 3.0 s, frames that arrive in 1.0 s and houses that build in 1.0 to 2.3 s and are blown away in 1.0 to 1.3 s, feature signs of 1.3 to 1.9 s, a 1.75 s caution-tape transition, a gold door that opens in 2.0 s, a paint pour of 4.3 s, day-evening-night changes of 2.0 s and a big win where each pig enters in 0.5 s and the wolf in 5.5 s. Acting is drawn frame by frame inside the rigs: the wolf's face up to 83 frames, pig loops of 25 to 29, two wind sequences of 136 and 165 half-screen frames. Sprite sheets state 24 frames a second. No skeleton frame is shown in this report: the project's drawing tool does not read Spine 4.1 correctly.
Money Gong EmperorSpine skeletons carry all of it: 16 skeletons in Spine 4.0 or 4.1 (the report header counts 30 files because 14 layout files of the client are counted with them). By their animation names: every symbol has a win, the money ball four landings, the gong turns like a coin to a feature face and is struck, pots grow and are hit by coins, firecrackers are lit and go off, four win tiers come in, loop and leave, and the emperor pops up with a scroll. Around them, 42 frame sequences (494 frames) of sparks, sweeps, trails and bursts, and nine particle files. No skeleton frame is shown: the project's drawing tool is written for Spine 3.7 and drew none of these; the six real screens show only the base game, the intro and a spin, so movement is read from names and parts and is inference throughout.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusAll motion is Spine: 41 skeletons in one bundle file (38 in 4.2.43; BonusSpinsSplash, ForegroundEffects and Foregrounds in 4.1.24) moving still pictures and cut-up characters, with 20 hand-drawn frame sequences (283 frames: the piggy coin's turn, plate bursts and sweeps in three materials, dust, wind, the wolf's breath, air rings and swirls on the tools, a frame glint, butterflies). Seen in play: the logo's words dropping in, the Boost sign growing across bleached reels and its word flying to a plate that flares and rises, a reel flashing pink under a landing Wild, winning symbols growing with a gold line, an air ring round the tape measure, a BIG WIN presented by the Straw Farmer pig. Not seen: the bonus, in which by the files the wolf inhales and blows (3.23 s) and the houses burst open. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer cannot draw Spine 4; assembled and motion pictures are absent for that reason only.
Zeus vs Hades POPSpine 3.7 skeletons carry almost all movement: symbols have landing (0.5 s), win (1.5 s) and sometimes idle and anticipation animations; the two mascots have six each (idle, idle break, two annoyed, two win). Fire, lightning, hair and sparkle are short hand-drawn frame sequences (3 to 21 frames) played inside the rigs. The expanding VS symbol plays as a duel with two outcomes, fire for Hades and lightning for Zeus. The scene transition is a video-like run of 25 full frames that shows Hades, then Zeus, then breaks open from the centre.
Variants
GameVariants
Cash EruptionOne hall in two brightnesses (base and free spins) and one separate bonus scene, which is also the loading picture. Reel backing in teal and red. Each symbol in three forms: a reel picture, a small paytable copy and a layered win version. In the free spins the three middle reels are linked and show one giant symbol, the same reel picture at three cells high. The fireball as a blank ball, with a live value, and with Mini, Minor or Major lettering. The wild as a one-cell bust and a three-cell standing figure. One button family (gold fret ring with a glass dome) in green, yellow, blue and red, each with lit and grey states.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandGrades by recolour on shared rigs: the saw in steel, diamond and gold; the wheel in silver and gold; features in plain, Super and Ultra; four houses on one rig. The hat and mansion blocks in 2x2, 3x3 and 3x5. English and Spanish versions of every worded picture. Landscape and portrait versions of most animations and plaques.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinThree backdrop states (base, cash bonus, jackpot bonus), two reel boards, six coin faces from one blank, two collectors from one train, two splash cards, three win tiers from one layout, fruit symbols from one fruit each with darker side copies.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinTwo states of the whole stage from one set of parts (normal and special skins: red for the base game, orange-gold with yellow beams for the Hold & Win, both seen in play); two states of every plate outline (resting and red); cash and jackpot plates as one component in two colours; three diamonds and two Boosters as recolours of one design each; desktop and mobile plate shapes; a brighter Add copy of almost every symbol for win flashes.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsTwo team colours on shared rigs: blue and red ball, blue and red goal. Three metals on one trophy rig and one frame set. Gold and super versions of the wheel wedges. The red ball as a 1x1, 2x2, 3x3 and 3x5 block. Day and night stadium on one drawing. English and Spanish versions of worded pictures. Landscape and portrait versions of most animations. Two control sets: the provider's grey one, used on the desktop screens, and a game-coloured one not seen in play.
Triple Cash EruptionOne cone, three colours; one fireball, four colours, each with a matching flame border; one flared serif, six colour codes. Every reel symbol ships as a still, a spin-blur copy and as layers (body, gold contour, shadow). Backgrounds and menus have landscape and portrait versions. The bonus buy offers two cards: a mystery card and a hotter super card.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelPink to gold is the upgrade rule for every pig (symbol, pot pig, wheel pig). The cash pig exists at 1x1, 2x2, 3x3 and 4x3. Scenes, panels and logos ship in landscape and portrait versions inside one pack; base and bonus versions of the board, wheel and prize panels differ by backing and glow. Win words ship in six languages. The client serves the same art at 0.5 and 0.75 of the studio's size; this run holds the 0.75 pack.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedTwo backdrop states (Normal, Special) for the ground and for each of eight 777 block views; one seven in four colourings (blue, purple, red, gold) and three counts; three jackpot plaques and three jackpot win plates from one idea; three win tiers and a total from one layout; lit and unlit paytable plates and numerals.
Capital GainsEvery symbol in three states: still, dimmed copy (drawn, about a quarter as bright) and animation. The Money Charge disc in 29 baked values, lit and dimmed. Reel window with a green or a red edge; background in green, red, paytable and loading versions. Titles with and without the word JACKPOTS, for markets without the jackpot. Only the desktop landscape layout was captured; the files name portrait cuts as well.
CleopatraTwo modes made by recolour: backdrop purple or crimson, cabinet window cream or tan, every symbol on a cream or tan ground, and each animated sequence shipped once per ground. Scatter in two words (SCATTER, BONUS), wild in two plates (DOUBLE, Cleopatra). Twenty bead colours and a grey. Buttons in four states. The client ships a desktop pack (symbols 244x244, backdrop 1920x1080, read here) and a mobile pack with the same art at half size in fewer atlases (symbols 122x122; captured first by mistake, see the record).
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarTwo scenes (bazaar, cave), each in landscape and portrait. Every symbol as a still and a blurred copy; picture symbols also as object and halo apart. One lamp design in three colours, one treasure pile in three sizes for each. One prize plaque in five titles, one numeral face in nine colourings. One button design in four states for every function. One bonus tile in blue and gold.
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinTwo states of the whole stage from two backdrops and one tinted board (skins normal and special; holdAndWin for the board): green for the base game, purple with coloured clovers and a rainbow ribbon for Free Spins (seen) and, by the skin names, the Hold & Win. Frame in two states (gold; white with rainbow glow). Pots in two states with a 14-frame change. One character at two crops (1x2 symbol and full reel). Five jackpot banners as two mirrored shapes in four colours plus the Grand. Splashes in a normal and an upgraded skin.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinTwo scenes on one picture (day, and a dusk regrade). Three Snakes on one rig with identical part sizes. Five jackpot plates on one shape, drawn twice (ladder size and win size). Three win tiers and a total on one lettering. Three collector frames told apart by gems and side lights. Two reel backings (five and six reels) and a frame cut in strips so the board grows from 5x4 to 6x6. Numerals in three coloured fonts.
Huff N Puff Money MansionThree times of day for the background and the prize plates. Three tiers of frame and house on one rig (straw, stick, brick). The hat at symbol size and as Mega Hat (the text names 2x2, 3x3 and 3x5). Reel frames in gold and blue-white for 3 and 4 rows. Every plaque, plate and number in a resting and a highlighted state. Three copies of the wolf (main, Major, Grand). Landscape and portrait versions of the transition.
Money Gong EmperorOne base ground, one curtain scene for the intro, and a board that changes backing from dark red to gold for the bonus spins; a Hold & Win grid and a round Money Gong Bonus wheel as feature scenes (parts only, not seen in play). Every reel symbol ships sharp and motion-blurred. The money ball comes green and gold, plain and with four jackpot names. The gong has five faces. Landscape only was captured; portrait animations are named in the files.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusTwo scenes on one composition (day building site, sunset village). Three pigs on one portrait layout and, by their parts, one rig. Three houses, each whole and destroyed. Three prize plates and three plate effects on one timing. Five jackpot names and five sets of coloured brick strips. Three win tiers and a total on one lettering. One numeral face in two colourings.
Zeus vs Hades POPNearly everything exists twice, as a blue base-game version and a red free-spins recolour: backgrounds, reel frame, backing, rails, bars, reel highlights and win-meter effects. Each reel symbol ships as a sharp still, a vertically smeared still (probably the spin blur: inference) and a skeleton. Win tiers are split between the gods: Zeus carries Mega and Sensational, Hades carries Nice and Superb. The three POP result banners (Burst magenta, Spark blue, Snap green) are one design recoloured.
Construction
GameConstruction
Cash Eruption621 named sprites on 67 textures, of which 56 units are the game's own art; 362 of the sprites are frames of 32 sequences. Sheets are in IGT's own view-builder format (a JSON of named sprites with frame rectangles beside each PNG, and a timeline file). Reel symbols are 558x500 pictures for a 261x238 cell. Backgrounds are single 1920x1080 JPEGs with no layers. The flame frames are repeated on each symbol sheet. Large light effects are small (the impact explosion is 96x96) and scaled up.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandPixiJS client. In this run: 140 textures, 1,535 named sprites, 11 skeletons, 3 fonts, 48 frame sequences. Sprite sheets are 'Red 7 Exporter' packs; skeletons are Spine 4.1.24 with few meshes and many additive slots; parts of one rig share one canvas size so grades, houses and banners swap part for part (saw parts 360x374, house parts 360x360, banner parts 1148x720). The background is one square 1920x1920 picture for both orientations. The reel board is a plain see-through dark rectangle with no drawn frame. The sign is a glTF model with a 1024x1024 texture; the wheel is assembled from wedge sprites.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinThree 4096 px atlas pages hold 532 sprites; backdrops are tall columns, the board and frames are mirrored halves, flames ship white to be tinted, words are separate from the coins and plaques they sit on. Five localised lettering files (en-GB). Paytable and buy-card pictures, the numeral font and the interface come from the provider's shared services.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinThree 4096 px atlas pages hold 391 sprites, more than half of them animation frames; there is no background picture at all (the backdrop is a 202 px white square and a glow circle, stretched and tinted). Symbols are layered: fruit in two halves, wild as button and word, Booster and Diamond as plate, object and word or bolt. Five localised lettering files (en-GB). The paytable pictures, logo copy, numeral fonts and interface come from the provider's shared services.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsPixiJS client. In this run: 168 textures, 1,702 named sprites, 12 skeletons, 8 fonts, 57 frame sequences holding 1,288 of the sprites. Sprite sheets are 'Red 7 Exporter' packs; skeletons are Spine 4.1 with few meshes (the wolf symbol has 19, most rigs none). Parts of one rig share a canvas size so colours and grades swap one for one (ball parts 336 to 338 px, trophy parts 278 px, goal parts 517x476). Each background is one square 1920x1920 picture for both orientations. The reel window is a plain see-through dark rectangle. File and animation names are those of the building-site Huff N' Puff games (woodcutter, hardhat, megahat, buzzsaw, houses, toolboxes): inference, this game was built by re-dressing that game's structure piece for piece.
Triple Cash EruptionThe 7 skeletons in the counts above are JSON files of a promotional overlay the demo host loads beside the game (listed under the provider interface, not read); the game's own 13 skeletons are binary files the tools do not count or draw. 76 textures and 1,913 named sprites were captured, 63 units of this game's art among them. Effects take most of the texture space: of 51 Spine atlas pages, 34 are opaque pages of frames on black (named _jpg, to be added as light) and several large effects ship as a colour page plus a black-and-white matte page instead of one page with alpha. The same small sequences are packed more than once (the hit burst three times, the embers twice), one copy per skeleton. Pages are WebP at quality 80 (as their names say), up to 2048 px. Symbol stills are about 150x130 px in a 180x158 cell.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelPixiJS client on Inspired's Virgo platform. 30 WebP atlas pages loaded of the 36 its manifest lists (the rest are other languages' win words and a US-CT wheel), up to 4096 px, packed by load order, not by subject, with trimmed and rotated frames listed in a packed manifest (base64 of LZ-UTF8 JSON), and all skeletons as JSON inside one data file. Symbols are small rigs of 4 to 30 parts with separate light layers; lettering is split into one sprite a letter where it must animate. Five of the pages are spent on the vault-door transition.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedThree 4096 px atlas pages hold 518 sprites, with two of the pages roughly half empty; the ground is a mirrored half; words are separate from what they label, and six lettering files are localised (en-GB). The paytable pictures, the help logo, the buy card, the numeral fonts, the Double Chance card, the controls and Poppins come from the provider's shared services. Compared with Fire Rail Express (run 2026-11-26-1556) from the files: the shell, Poppins and the Double Chance card are the same; 40 sprites are pixel for pixel the same (36 white flame frames, the white starburst, a glow, a glow square, a white box); 23 of the 46 skeleton names are the same (Backgrounds, Logo, SlotFrame, Jackpot, WinBig, WinTotal, TileWild and others), which points to one scene template; the pictures under shared names such as bgNormal, bgSpecial and jackpotFrame are different. Everything that carries the theme is this game's own.
Capital Gains29 texture pages, 1,188 named sprites in TexturePacker atlases, one atlas per symbol animation and one per screen (base game, preloader, paytable, vault gateway, Money Charge, menus, autoplay). Backgrounds are four JPEGs at 1440x810. Everything is a bitmap or a frame sequence; values and pay rows are baked pictures; labels and meters are live text. The console and the autoplay panel are a neutral dark kit that is not themed to the game.
CleopatraA small package: 19 textures, 705 named sprites, 14 frame sequences with 611 frames, 2 fonts. Every atlas is a TexturePacker JSON with the studio's own names. Symbols are untrimmed opaque 244x244 cells with the ground baked in; the cabinet is one 1645x1080 picture per mode with the window painted in and a divider grid laid over the symbols; the backdrop is one mirrored JPEG per mode. Mode differences are made by whole second copies, not by layers or tints: 320 of the 611 animation frames are the wild, and half of all animation frames exist only to change a cell margin from cream to tan. Text is live, so the art holds no language.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret Bazaar987 named sprites on 54 atlas pages (1,011 components and 77 textures with the fonts, loose pictures and the demo host's overlay), 43 frame sequences holding 664 frames, 4 embedded fonts of the game. The client served its sheets from a folder named mobile: symbol cells are 164x145 and buttons 200x200, close to what a 1280x720 screen shows, while backgrounds are 2040x1410. Whether a larger pack exists for other devices is not known from this capture. Art is split by blend, not by subject: each skeleton has a page of opaque plates for additive light and a page with alpha. Greyscale and white effect art is tinted in the engine. Much is pre-rendered from 3D (gem turns, tile tumbles, word swings, coin flips) rather than rigged.
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinTwo 4096 px atlas pages hold 442 sprites, 290 of them animation frames, with 18 localised lettering files (en-GB), six loose textures and one skeleton bundle. The two backdrops are 1375x1255 pictures; the reel board ships in grey and is tinted. Symbols are layered where they move (mug in ten parts, Booster in four, coins with turn and shine frames) and single pictures where they do not (royals, the four props). Paytable pictures, the flattened logo, the numeral fonts and the interface come from the provider's shared services.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinThree 4096 px atlas pages hold the game: two carry one 2750x2510 scene each with the large pieces, the third some 600 small sprites. Eleven word pictures are localised (en-GB). Characters are few and cheap: the statue is one still with glow layers, a Snake is seven parts, the screen-filling wipe is six 307 px scale strips run along a path. Water moves by a displacement map over a mask, not by frames. White effect sprites are tinted in the engine. Symbol pictures for the help, the flat logo, the numeral fonts, the Extra Chance card, the controls and Poppins come from the provider's shared store outside the game bundle. The artists' green cell guide (tileGuide) ships in the atlas as an anchor.
Huff N Puff Money MansionPixiJS client. In this run: 349 textures, 3,579 named sprites, 19 skeletons, 3 fonts, 107 frame sequences (3,189 frames). Sprite sheets are 'Red 7 Exporter' packs; skeletons are Spine 4.1.24 with few bones (4 to 62) and most of their weight in frame sequences played inside the rig. Parts of one rig share a canvas so tiers swap part for part (house parts 302x303 and 352x351, symbol parts 336x336). The mansion is a 1920x1920 picture per time of day over a 1920x2472 sky. The reel board is a see-through dark panel in a hairline frame. Atlas pages are 2048x2048; the three wolf rigs take 132 of them and the prize meters 54.
Money Gong Emperor1,127 named sprites on 54 textures in 51 units, 49 of them the game's own art. Solid art is PNG in TexturePacker sheets or Spine atlases; effects are JPEG on black on separate pages of the same atlas; backgrounds are single JPEGs with no layers (1584x720, the curtain 3168x1440). A reel symbol is about 300x270 for a cell of about 313x302; the emperor of the pop-up is the largest art (head 899x801). Half of the reel frame is shipped and mirrored (inference). Three skeletons (the two ambients and the transition) ship only a placeholder.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusTwo 4096 px atlas pages hold 453 sprites, each page carrying one 2750 px scene; four lettering files are localised (en-GB). Characters and houses are cut into parts for Spine (the wolf 43 sprites with breath, the pigs 32, the houses 33). The reel backing and its pig watermark are grey and tinted by the engine. The flat symbol pictures, the flat logo, the numeral fonts, the Extra Chance card, the controls and Poppins come from the provider's shared store, outside the game bundle.
Zeus vs Hades POP3,550 named sprites on 243 textures, 39 skeletons. A character is 73 to 221 parts, with a painted shadow piece for nearly every overlapping part and separate additive glow layers; meshes are used for cloth, hair and faces, regions for rigid parts. The four royals share one 9 to 10 part template: a coloured letter face with flickering lightning at rest, and a lava-cell picture that fills the face, clipped to the letter, during the win. Atlas textures are shipped at 50 to 69% of the source art and as 8-bit palette PNGs. The reel board is deliberately plain (flat backing, thin frame, gold dividers); the prize bar is its one decorated piece.
Consistency
GameConsistency
Cash EruptionTight in colour and ornament, loose in manner. The red-gold-teal palette and the step-fret hold everything together, which lets three rendering styles (toy fruit, photographic fire, pin-up figure) sit on one board. The bonus backdrop is the one piece in a different hand: flat and posterised against the rendered hall.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandHigh: one outline-and-gloss treatment on every object, one lettering system, one colour per prize tier (blue-white for the top: Ultra, diamond saw, mansion frame), and the building-site motif carried into signs, stripes and the transition. The Buy Pass dialog's buttons are the one generic-looking set. The wolf's howling-moon win picture is a deliberate change of register.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinHigh. Gold, the flame emblem and the slab serif recur on every piece, and the ticket shape returns as logo, particle and backdrop. The one seam is between the rendered-look objects and the flat engraved postcards, and it is used on purpose as foreground against background.
Mega Cash Boost Hold And WinVery high: one slant, three shapes and three prize colours run through backdrop, frame, plates, symbols, lettering and effects. The only seam is between the softly painted fruit and the hard graphic world around it, and the blue rim on the fruit is there to close it.
Huff N Lots Of GoalsHigh: one outline-and-gloss treatment on every object, one lettering system, one colour per prize tier, one cream smoke for every puff, and red against blue carried from the symbols to the goals, the pig's face paint and the transition. The wolf is drawn flatter than the painted symbols, a deliberate cel-cartoon register. The provider's grey controls and help pages are the one part outside the theme.
Triple Cash EruptionStrong where it matters: the colour code is never broken, teal with gold is every number plate, the flared serif is every label. Three hands show otherwise: glossy rounded symbols, flat poster backgrounds and one soft painterly vortex behind the panels, and they are kept apart by where they appear, so they do not clash.
Bigger Piggy Bank SuperwheelThe pig-and-money art is tight: one light, one finish, one lettering hand, one mark. The Super Wheel, its red interface and the gamble wheel are visibly a second system (flat fills, block capitals, red glow buttons), dressed with the logo and a snout coin but not redrawn in the toy style.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedVery high, by economy: one seven, one letter style, three hues and gold. The one piece outside the system is the painted buy card, and it shows the same cast.
Capital GainsVery consistent and very narrow: one rendering manner for every object, one green for the world, gold for value, blue lightning for the feature. The console is the one foreign body, grey-violet and unthemed. The feature's brand (Money Charge Jackpots, violet and yellow) deliberately does not match the game's green and gold, so it reads as a badge shared across games (inference).
CleopatraThe identity is tight where it matters: one face and one wordmark serve as key art, logo and wild, and gold with lotus ornament runs through symbols, cabinet and plaques. Around that the manners differ openly: outlined comic face, airbrushed objects, flat Sphinx, smooth vector-like cabinet, tinted photo backdrop, naturalistic fire, and generic blue and red web buttons for autospin. The game reads as one because of its strict grid, its gold and its single counter-colour, not because the rendering is uniform.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarHigh. One palette rule (red and gold board, violet controls, magenta for wins), one material set and one binding motif, smoke, run from the loading picture to the smallest effect. The lettering is the loosest part: five display faces share only their gold. Two file names for symbols do not match their pictures, a trace of an earlier symbol set (inference).
The Lucky Fella Hold And WinHigh. One clover module, one gold, one rainbow and one wobbling line run through backdrop, frame, symbols, interface and effects, and the green rim light ties the painted props to the green field. Seams: the win-tier lettering (dark with a neon outline) and the flat cartoon smoke are drawn in other hands than the gold-and-enamel world around them, and the white bursts are generic.
Serpent Gold Hold And WinStrong inside each register, with one visible seam between them: the soft photoreal jungle and the hard enamel game pieces do not share light or edge quality, and the birds, painted sharper than the scene, sit between. The seam is used rather than hidden: the dark board and gold rims make every symbol read at once against the haze. Colour coding is exact across symbol, frame, word and effect. The comic-capital win words are the least themed element.
Huff N Puff Money MansionHigh: one outline-and-gloss treatment on every object, one lettering system, one colour per prize tier, and the building-site motif carried into symbols, signs, the transition, the feature props and the logo. Two things stand apart: the wolf and the big-win pigs are animated as whole frames while everything else is parts and overlays, and one stray sequence (a fire dragon) belongs to another game. Part names left from the earlier Huff N' Puff games (buzzsaw, wheel) show the rigs were carried over and re-dressed (inference).
Money Gong EmperorVery tight. One emblem at four sizes, two ornaments, one top light and a two-colour palette hold every screen together, and the few other colours are a code the player learns on the intro panel and meets again on the gong, the balls and the meters. The loose ends are the neutral grey buttons and the plain sans win titles, which belong to the provider's kit more than to the game.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusVery consistent: one idea (three materials in rising strength) orders the Wilds, houses, ladders, win tiers and effects, and one mark (the snout) themes every filler symbol. The joins that show are between the painted characters and the flat glossy letters, which are two different finishes on the same reel, and the plain gold reel frame, which belongs to neither. Shared with the other Octoplay runs (Fire Rail Express, 777 Hot Reels): the shell, Poppins, the Extra Chance card `buyChances2x` (the same file) and three light sprites (circularWhiteRays2, glowSquare, whiteGlow, pixel for pixel); 22 and 24 of the 41 skeleton names also appear in those runs, one scene template (inference). A sprite reading BOILERPLATE is left in the atlas.
Zeus vs Hades POPThe Greek set is tight: one rendering manner, one frame construction, one gold. Three things sit outside it and look like shared platform art or a different hand: the POP bubble symbol and banners (glossy candy style), the flat gold title plates in the big-win atlas, and loose shared sprites such as number fonts, coins and a red envelope (inference).

Next steps in art

Three more reports (September, October and November 2026 editions) were handled after this was written. They add 27 leaders that are being analysed now. This text still describes the sixteen games analysed from the July and August editions and is written again when the new leaders are settled.

Written 27 Nov 2026. These are recommendations, not findings: each is our inference from the sixteen analysed leaders, and names the games it rests on. Art of the leaders holds the evidence. They are written for the studio's AI art work (the Games AI art project: a reference game's art out, our own theme's art in, and the agentic test against what our artists delivered).

Read this first. The evidence covers IGT, Octoplay, Light & Wonder, AGS and Inspired. Fourteen of the 30 leaders, including all eight of Games Global's, could not be analysed. A recommendation here says "the leaders we could open do this", not "the market does this". The first step below is about closing that gap.

In short

  1. Close the evidence gap before leaning on these conclusions: the Games Global games, and the bonus rounds we did not see.
  2. Start every game's art from a written colour code and one emblem, before any picture is made.
  3. Compose the base game around the prize, on a dark, plain reel window.
  4. Plan the art package as stills plus a shared effects kit, and use generated art where the leaders' own art is stills.
  5. Make feature modes and tiers by recolour, regrade and swap, and brief them as sets.
  6. Treat a new theme on a proven frame as a normal way to make a game.
  7. Take one or both of two looks into a concept: the classic machine re-dressed, and the glossy cartoon cast.
  8. Build the tool pieces that limited this study, a Spine 4.x renderer first.

1. Close the evidence gap

  • Games Global (8 leaders). Every public demo refused this container because its traffic leaves from the United States. Either run the capture from a studio machine in a country the demos serve, or ask the product team for demo links. This is the largest hole in the picture.
  • White Hat Studios (2 leaders). No public demo. A sibling of each opens on Blueprint Gaming's demo server (Cash Strike Hotstepper 2, Cash Strike Power Force 5); that they are the same games under European names is inference. Decide whether they may stand in, labelled as stand-ins.
  • Aristocrat, Evolution, ReelPlay, IGT's Cash Eruption High Stakes (4 leaders). Each needs a link or an account from the product team.
  • Bonus rounds not seen. A played session of one to two hours per game, or the provider's own test tools where the studio has them, would turn "read from the files" into "seen" for Super Cash Boost, The Lucky Fella, Money Gong Emperor, Bigger Piggy Bank and the three Huff N Puff games.

2. Begin with a colour code and one emblem

Do: make the first page of every art brief a table, written before any image is generated: one colour per prize tier, one per feature, one for "money won", and the surfaces each must appear on (symbol, frame, plaque, effect, win word, buy card). Add one emblem or mark and the list of pieces that carry it.

Why: this is the most consistent thing the analysed leaders do. Colour names the feature or the tier everywhere in Triple Cash Eruption, Serpent Gold, Mega Cash Boost, 777 Hot Reels Megacharged, Mystery Of The Lamp and all three Huff N Puff games. One emblem or mark ties plain objects into one game in Money Gong Emperor (the gong), Bigger Piggy Bank (the snout) and The Lucky Fella (the clover).

For generated art in particular: a fixed code is what keeps separately generated pieces looking like one game. The 777 Hot Reels analysis names the hues that would have to be fixed first (#0b37b7 blue, #c366f7 purple, #c50b05 red, #f9c013 gold); our briefs should carry the same kind of line.

In the agentic test: add "colour code held" to what reviewers check. A generated package can score well piece by piece and still break the code.

3. Compose around the prize, on a dark plain board

Do: treat the base-game layout as a brief of its own, with three fixed decisions.

  • The reel window is dark and plain, and every symbol has one colour of its own (a tile, a cloth, a halo or a rim). Rests on Capital Gains, Cleopatra, Mystery Of The Lamp, Bigger Piggy Bank and Serpent Gold.
  • Warm symbols, cool ground (or the reverse), decided on purpose. Rests on Cash Eruption, Triple Cash Eruption and Huff N Even More Puff Grand.
  • The top prizes and the feature's progress are in the picture from the first spin, as an object that changes: a wheel behind the reels, goals that fill, a statue that heats, a house front that is the prize board. Rests on the three Huff N Puff games, Serpent Gold, Mega Cash Boost, Mystery Of The Lamp and Triple Cash Eruption.

Do not spend on scenery first. None of the sixteen puts its budget into a landscape, and five have no scene at all (Capital Gains, Money Gong Emperor, Cleopatra, Mega Cash Boost, The Lucky Fella).

4. Stills plus a kit: where generated art fits

The analysts were asked to say, game by game, what an AI art pipeline could make. Their answers agree.

PieceFit for generated artRests on
Backgrounds, and a second scene by regradeGood. This is where an image model gives most.Serpent Gold, Super Cash Boost, Mystery Of The Lamp
Symbol stills (objects, fruit, still-life wares)Good, when the colour code and finish are fixed firstCapital Gains, Cleopatra, Mystery Of The Lamp, Fire Rail Express
A character as one strong still, cut into a few partsReachableCash Eruption, Money Gong Emperor, Fire Rail Express
Character variants on one layout (three pigs, three snakes)Reachable, as a consistency briefSuper Cash Boost, Serpent Gold
Glows, masks, dimmed and blurred copiesDerive from the stills; do not generateMoney Gong Emperor, Capital Gains, Bigger Piggy Bank
Short fire, burst and sparkle loops on black or in whitePossible; colour consistency across frames is the risk, which is why the leaders ship them white and tintTriple Cash Eruption, Fire Rail Express
Frames, plates, lettering, ornamentNeeds tight art direction: exact shape language and clean edgesSerpent Gold, Mystery Of The Lamp
Acted sequences, destruction, windAn animator's jobthe three Huff N Puff games
3D transitions (a vault door, turning gems)A 3D render jobBigger Piggy Bank, Mystery Of The Lamp

Do:

  • Define the static package as a list of stills, per game, in the brief. The Huff N Puff analyses give the scale: one or two backgrounds, 16 to 18 symbol stills at about 300 px, a set of tiered objects with frames and backings, a coin, wedges and plates, a logo.
  • Build one studio effects kit in white: sparkle, smoke, burst, lightning and flame loops, tinted per game. Half of The Lucky Fella's drawn frames and more than half of Mega Cash Boost's are such effects, and 777 Hot Reels Megacharged reuses another game's flame files.
  • Take "a still plus overlays" as the first motion target, before rigs: reel picture, outline glow, spark and one loop, as in Cash Eruption. Two leaders ship no rig at all (Capital Gains, Cleopatra).
  • Plan each symbol's outputs up front: still, dimmed copy, blurred copy, additive light copy. Each of these appears in several leaders, and all can be derived from the still.
  • Cut for animation from the start. A breakable symbol is one painting, 14 shards, two crack overlays and an "inside" picture (Bigger Piggy Bank); a house exists whole and in pieces (Super Cash Boost).
  • Keep words out of pictures. Words separate from coins, plaques and splashes make localisation a handful of files (all six Octoplay games), and they also spare an image model from drawing letters.

5. Brief modes and tiers as sets

Do: ask for variants as a set in one brief, never one by one.

  • A feature mode is the same composition recoloured or regraded: "day and dusk of one picture" (Serpent Gold, Super Cash Boost, Huff N Lots Of Goals), or one hue flipped while the board stays (777 Hot Reels Megacharged, Capital Gains, Cleopatra).
  • A tier is the same object in another material at the same canvas size: straw, stick, brick; steel, diamond, gold; pink, gold (Huff N Even More Puff Grand, Huff N Puff Money Mansion, Bigger Piggy Bank).
  • Neutral art tinted in the engine where a mode only changes colour: a grey reel board (The Lucky Fella, Super Cash Boost).

For the tools: this is a natural next piece of the concept step. Given one approved still, produce its regrade, its material swaps and its dimmed, blurred and light copies at fixed sizes, and measure that each stays inside the colour code.

6. A new theme on a proven frame

Do: treat re-dressing a working game as a first-class way to make a new one, and say so in the plan.

Why: Huff N Lots Of Goals ranks among the leaders and, by its file names, is the building-site game with football art in every slot (inference). The six Octoplay leaders stand on one framework and share almost no picture. 777 Hot Reels Megacharged is a "charged" version made from two logo words, 25 lightning frames and a jackpot row.

This is what the studio's concept step already does: it takes a reference game's extracted package and fills it piece for piece with our own theme's art. The leaders show the same method in production. The art package extracted from each analysed game is such a frame, with every piece named and sized.

Mind the seam. A shared feature left in another finish looks bolted on (Bigger Piggy Bank's wheel). When a piece is reused across our games, redraw its surface in the game's finish.

7. Two looks worth a concept each

These are suggestions for what to try, not predictions of what will sell. The market reports rank games; they do not say why a game ranks.

  • The classic machine, re-dressed. Seven of the sixteen analysed leaders keep fruit, sevens, letters or money icons plain and put the art into one money object and one effect family. Their static art is small (a 3x3 or 5x3 set, one emblem, a plaque set), which suits a first fully generated package. References: Cash Eruption, Fire Rail Express, Mega Cash Boost.
  • The glossy cartoon cast. Six of the sixteen, five of them on pigs. It needs consistent characters and acted animation, so it tests the harder half of the pipeline. References: Super Cash Boost for a lean version, Huff N Even More Puff Grand for the full one.

8. Tool work this study asks for

In order of what it would unlock:

  1. A Spine 4.x renderer. Twelve of the sixteen games use Spine 4.0 to 4.2 and none of their rigs could be drawn. Until then no skeleton frame of such a game is published.
  2. Readers for three provider formats, now living as per-run scripts: Light & Wonder's sheets (three runs carry a copy of the same script), Octoplay's skeleton bundle and packed pages, Inspired's packed manifests. Each belongs in the extraction tool.
  3. A capture that waits for the game, not for a clock, and a play driver that can scroll a paytable and hold a long session. Loading took from under a minute to 35 minutes across these games.
  4. Measures by art component, not over the whole package, so one character's frames cannot swing a game's palette (Huff N Puff Money Mansion).
  5. A build audit for our own packages: duplicate sequences, near-identical rigs and stray files, the waste found in Huff N Puff Money Mansion, Triple Cash Eruption and Bigger Piggy Bank.

Decisions for Roei

  • A machine outside the United States, or demo links, for the eight Games Global leaders?
  • May the Blueprint siblings stand in for the two White Hat Studios leaders?
  • Longer played sessions, or a provider's test tools, for the bonus rounds not seen?
  • A Drive folder and a Miro board for each of the sixteen new runs, as the earlier Games AI art runs have? None was made.
  • Which of the two looks in step 7, if either, to take into a concept first.

Method

How a market report becomes this ledger. Every step is a tool in the repository IntelligateStudios/market-reports-handler; the procedure is its skill handle-market-report.

1. The report is taken

The PDF is copied in unchanged, with each page's text, a picture of each page and the tables found on it. A PDF taken before is recognised by its fingerprint and is not taken twice.

2. Its rankings are read

Every ranked list in the report is written down as the report prints it: the list's title, what it measures, the market, the page, and each game's rank, provider and value. Nothing is added to a list, and a value appears only as the report states it.

3. The games are joined to the record

Each ranked name is matched to the one ledger of games: the same title from the same provider is the same game, whatever the spelling, capitals or marks. A sequel or a version ("1000", "Megaways", "Xmas") is a game of its own. A name that could be two games is never guessed: the run stops until someone decides.

The ledger started from what the studio already had: the games with a PRD and GDD in Intelligate HQ, the games of our web research of 21 Nov 2026, and the art runs in Games AI art.

4. The report's 20 leaders are fixed

Only slot games count. With one list, the leaders are its first 20. With several lists, a game earns 21 − rank points in each list that ranks it in the first 20 (times the list's weight, 1 unless the run's record says why not), and the 20 highest totals lead. This rule is ours, a way to join a report's lists into one order. It is not a figure of the report, and each report's page shows its lists unchanged beside it.

5. Each leader is analysed once

A leader with no art analysis gets one: a run of Games AI art on the provider's public free-play demo, which extracts every texture, sprite and skeleton, measures every image and reads every art component. Its full report is published as its own page and linked here. A game analysed for an earlier report is not analysed again; its page simply gains the new report's rank. A game that cannot be analysed (no public demo, a client the tools cannot read) is marked Blocked with the reason.

6. The two documents are written

When every leader is analysed or blocked, two documents are written from the finished analyses: Art of the leaders, the games' art side by side, and Next steps in art, what Intelligate should do next, each recommendation resting on named games.

Measured or read

LabelWhat it means
MeasuredComputed from the game's own pixels by fixed rules, the same for every game, so two games can be compared: palette and shares, brightness, saturation, contrast, warm and cool share, soft edges.
ReadWritten by Claude from looking at the game's sheets and screens: style, rendering, lighting, ambience, materials. Inference is marked as inference.
As statedCopied from a market report, with its page.

Limits

  • A report's ranking is that publisher's view of its own markets and period; two reports can disagree, and both are kept.
  • An art analysis covers the layout and the features the demo showed during the capture, at the size the game ships its art.
  • Competitors' art is kept for study inside the studio and is not shared outside it.
